title: vercel-labs /agent-browser
summary:
agent-browser Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell. agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. snapshot returns the page as compact text with a ref such as @e1 for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call. Install npm install -g agent-browser
agent-browser install # download Chrome for Testing (first time only) Homebrew: brew install agent-browser , then agent-browser install . Linux: agent-browser install --with-deps also installs the browser's system libraries. No install: npx agent-browser open example.com . Project installs, building from source, upgrade , and doctor are covered in Installation . Quick start agent-browser open example.com
agent-browser snapshot -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-browser click @e1 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-browser get url # check the result agent-browser close The snapshot for example.com : - link "Learn more" [ref=e1] Refs describe the page at the time of the snapshot. After navigation or a DOM change, take a new snapshot before using refs again. CSS selectors, text, XPath, and semantic locators also work, for example agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit" . See Selectors . A click fails, instead of reporting success, when the target is hidden, disabled, outside the viewport, or covered by another element such as a consent banner. Dismiss the covering element, take a new snapshot, and retry. The full walkthrough is in the quick start . How it works The CLI sends each command to a background daemon that starts on the first command and controls the browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Each --session gets its own daemon and browser. By default, the daemon closes a headless browser and exits after one hour without comm

title: meta /astryx
summary:
Astryx An open source design system that's fully customizable and built for how we build now: by people and the agents working alongside them. Currently in Beta · Built on React 19+ and StyleX Docs · Storybook · Sandbox · Contributing · Discord Overview Astryx is an open source design system that grew inside Meta over the last eight years, where it became the most-used and largest design system in the company — powering 13,000+ apps and shaped by the engineers, designers, and product teams who depend on it every day. It ships 150+ accessible components, brand-level theming, dark mode, ready-to-ship templates, and a CLI as one cohesive system. You import pre-built CSS and use typed React components — no build plugin, no styling library to adopt — and both people and AI assistants build with the same tooling. What makes Astryx different: Open internals. Components are built to be composed at any level, not locked behind a closed top-level API. The building blocks you'd reach for are exported directly, and when you need to go deeper, swizzle ejects a component's full source into your project to own. No styling lock-in. Astryx authors its styles with StyleX, but that's invisible to consumers. Override with className using Tailwind, CSS modules, or plain CSS — whatever your project already uses. Customize without wrapping. A theme is a set of CSS custom property overrides, so a designer can make Astryx unmistakably theirs without forking or wrapping component source. Built for people and agents. The API, docs, and CLI are designed together so a person and an AI assistant build the same way, from the same reference. Getting Started Astryx requires React 19 or later ( react and react-dom are peer dependencies of @astryxdesign/core ). Install Astryx, a theme, and its peer dependencies: # npm npm install @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex
npm install -D @astryxdesign/cli # pnpm pnpm add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/sty

summary: Note: This repository contains Anthropic's implementation of skills for Claude. For information about the Agent Skills standard, see agentskills.io . Skills teach Claude how to complete specific tasks in a repeatable way, whether that's creating documents with your company's brand guidelines, analyzing data using your organization's specific workflows, or automating personal tasks. For more information, check out: What are skills? Using skills in Claude How to create custom skills Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills About This Repository This repository contains skills that demonstrate what's possible with Claude's skills system. Each skill is self-contained in its own folder with a SKILL.md file containing the instructions and metadata that Claude uses. Browse through these skills to get inspiration for your own skills or to understand different patterns and approaches. Many skills in this repo are open source (Apache 2.0). We've also included the document creation & editing skills that power Claude's document capabilities under the hood in the skills/docx , skills/pdf , skills/pptx , and skills/xlsx subfolders. title: anthropics /claude-quickstarts
summary: Claude Quickstarts Claude Quickstarts is a collection of projects designed to help developers quickly get started with building  applications using the Claude API. Each quickstart provides a foundation that you can easily build upon and customize for your specific needs. Getting Started To use these quickstarts, you'll need an Claude API key. If you don't have one yet, you can sign up for free at console.anthropic.com . Available Quickstarts Customer Support Agent A customer support agent powered by Claude. This project demonstrates how to leverage Claude's natural language understanding and generation capabilities to create an AI-assisted customer support system with access to a knowledge base. Go to Customer Support Agent Quickstart Financial Data Analyst A financial data analyst powered by Claude. This project demonstrates how to leverage Claude's capabilities with interactive data visualization to analyze financial data via chat. Go to Financial Data Analyst Quickstart Computer Use Demo An environment and tools that Claude can use to control a desktop computer. This project demonstrates how to leverage the computer use capabilities of Claude, including support for the latest computer_toolset_20260801 toolset shape, where each computer action is a member tool the model calls by name. Go to Computer Use Demo Quickstart Computer Use Best Practices A pedagogical, native-macOS reference implementation of a computer-use agent. Unlike the containerized Computer Use Demo, this project runs directly against the macOS desktop (run it in a VM!) and demonstrates common patterns for building more reliable and cost-effective computer-use agents: explicit tool definitions, correct image sizing and pruning, prompt caching, server-side compaction, batched tool calls, a sandboxed shell, and trajectory recording. It pairs with Anthropic's computer-use best-practices guide . Go to Computer Use Best Practices Quickstart Browser Use Demo A complete reference implementation for browse

title: I merged attention and MLP processing into a single gated Transformer block. GAP [R]
summary: Hi everyone!I've been experimenting with an alternative Transformer architecture calledGAP (Gated Attention Projection).The main idea is to combine attention and MLP-style processing into a single gated block, instead of using the standard separate attention and feed-forward sublayers.I tested it against a standard Transformer using 100 million scored training tokens per model from WikiText-103.Some results:GAP20 used19.91% fewer parametersthan the standard Transformer.A smaller configuration can reduce parameters by34.31%, although that version did not fair as well as the current model against the regular transformer, so i ended up giving 14% of my perameters savings to the GAP model for extra width, leaving the model at about 20% fewer perameters, which is why i called it in testing GAP20The standard Transformer performed better on final language-model accuracy.Compiling GAP20 with torch.compile improved training throughput by approximately19.9%in one CPU benchmark compared with running GAP20 without compilation.I've included the architecture code, configurable model sizes, speed benchmark and research paper.This is an experimental architecture, not a claim that it outperforms Transformers overall. I'd be interested in feedback on the design, mathematics and possible improvements.GitHub:https://github.com/rickey1990/Gated-Attention-Projectionsubmitted by/u/WAMFT[link][comments]
title_es: GAP: alternativa experimental de Transformer más eficiente en parámetros
bajada: Un investigador propuso GAP (Gated Attention Projection), una arquitectura de Transformer alternativa que fusiona procesamiento de atención y MLP en un solo bloque gateado. GAP logró reducir parámetros en un 20% manteniendo rendimiento comparable, aunque con mejoras marginales en compilación.
bajada_en: A researcher proposed GAP (Gated Attention Projection), an alternative Transformer architecture that combines attention and MLP processing in a single gated block. GAP achieved a 20% parameter reduction while maintaining comparable performance, with marginal compilation improvements.

title: How agentic AI raises the bar for law firms
summary: The legal world is looking to scale AI beyond chatbots, bringing in agents to automate parts of lawyers’ workflows. While adoption is growing rapidly, some firms are moving slower than others. Laura Mandaro, managing editor at The Information, talked to three legal experts about how firms can overcome pushback, encourage adoption and measure AI’s returns.Isabel Parker, Chief Innovation Officer, White & CaseJillian Burnett, VP Engagement, LegoraSunita Verma, CTO, IroncladThe agent advantageAt many law firms, drafting non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) are a time sink. Sunita Verma of Ironclad, an AI-driven contract management company, said this is a workflow that can easily be outsourced to an agent.“One of the themes we hear consistently from our customers is that they want their lawyers spending less time on NDAs and more time on strategic deals,” she said. For some clients that have outsourced NDAs to AI, the time saved has made it possible to bring work previously handled by external legal providers in-house.But not every law firm has embraced AI. Isabel Parker said that while lawyers at White & Case were comfortable using AI for basics like summarizing documents, most remained resistant to a wider rollout of agents.The firm does use agents to improve client experiences, mostly through client-specific skills that capture preferences, from tone of voice to who needs to be included on contracts and communications. The skills make institutional knowledge easier to share.“In the past, a lawyer might say, ‘I’m about to submit this to X client, how do they like to see it again? Has anyone written this down?’ And emails would be flying around and everyone’s hair on fire,” Parker said. “This makes it much more streamlined.”Getting lawyers on boardJillian Burnett acknowledges that skepticism from lawyers can be a barrier to adopting agentic tools like Legora, the agentic operating system for legal work. bajada_en: NVIDIA researchers and partners demonstrated that simulation enables robots to learn complex manipulation tasks like gear alignment and cable connection. This advance expands the potential of autonomous robots beyond locomotion.

title: New Fireworks Hack Threatens $1 Billion Business
summary: Fireworks, a startup that helps developers run and train open-source models, in the last week has told some of its large customers including Harvey of a recent, more serious hack to its systems, according to two people with knowledge of the breach. The hack exposed data from some Fireworks customers, the company said Monday.Now some of Fireworks’ customers, who spend millions of dollars on its services per year, are considering switching to other providers, one of the people said. The incident highlights the increased security risks companies face, as AI-powered breaches become more common.
title_es: NVIDIA y Corea expanden colaboración en IA soberana
bajada: NVIDIA y el Ministerio de Ciencia de Corea ampliaron su colaboración en ecosistema de IA soberana, incluyendo semiconductores, infraestructura de datos y desarrollo de agentes. La alianza posiciona a compañías coreanas en el ecosistema NVIDIA NVLink Fusion.
bajada_en: NVIDIA and South Korea's Ministry of Science expanded collaboration on sovereign AI ecosystem, including semiconductors, data center infrastructure, and agent development. The alliance positions Korean companies within the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion ecosystem.

title_es: Agentes de IA transforman workflows en despachos jurídicos
bajada: Bufetes de abogados están escalando IA más allá de chatbots, adoptando agentes que automatizan flujos como redacción de NDAs y análisis de contratos. Aunque la adopción crece, hay variabilidad en la velocidad de implementación entre firmas.
bajada_en: Law firms are scaling AI beyond chatbots, adopting agents that automate workflows like NDA drafting and contract analysis. While adoption is growing, implementation speed varies significantly across firms.

title_es: El debate sobre data centers es fundamentalmente sobre electricidad
bajada: Análisis de MIT Tech Review revela que la resistencia a nuevos data centers se centra principalmente en preocupaciones de consumo energético, no solo en privacidad. Este enfoque redefine la conversación sobre infraestructura de IA.
bajada_en: MIT Tech Review analysis reveals that resistance to new data centers centers primarily on energy consumption concerns, not just privacy. This focus reframes the conversation about AI infrastructure.
